headline: TWO FESTIVALS. ONE COAST.
dek: Carnival in Nice. Citrus floats in Menton.
accessibility_angle: One Nice base and separate TER outings; allow for festival crowds and station-to-centre walking. No step-free or quiet-retreat claim.
editorial_intent: An event-led February 2027 Riviera rail break: stay in Nice, anchor dates around Carnival and Menton's Lemon Festival, then choose food, art and harbour outings between events.
share_reason: Save the overlapping festival window, know which events to book first, understand east/west train directions, and choose specific food and art stops.
reader_scenario: A pair or small group uses Nice as a base for several days, selecting one town per outing rather than rushing through all four in a day.
editorial_verdict: Accepted: a concrete car-free coastal holiday with verified rail links and a mix of city seafront, ramparts, village lanes and sheltered bay. Summer imagery is explicitly planning inspiration, not a November weather promise.
caption:
The French Riviera's best reason for a February trip might be a parade made of lemons. 🍋

In 2027, Nice Carnival runs 9–28 February and Menton's Fête du Citron runs 13–28 February. Your shared festival window: 13–28 February. One Nice base, two spectacles, coastal trains between them.

Book the event first. Menton's programme lists Golden Fruit Parades on 14, 21 and 28 February, night parades on 18 and 25 February, and citrus displays in the Biovès gardens throughout the festival. Nice's flower battles and carnival floats are the other draw; confirm individual performance dates and tickets with the organisers.

Between events: buy hot socca at Cours Saleya in Nice; pair Antibes' Picasso Museum and sculpture terrace with its sea walls; or take Villefranche's old lanes down to Cocteau's painted Saint-Pierre chapel by the harbour.

Antibes lies WEST of Nice. Villefranche and Menton lie EAST. Pick one outing per day, leaving room to return for an evening event. Check last TER trains, museum opening days and closures before fixing the plan. February is for festivals, food and sea air; sunny coastal photos are location views, not a swimming forecast.

Save this before the group chat books another summer-only Riviera trip.

Photos: Luna Wang, Nick Page, Pix Tresa, Anatoli Nicolae, Artem R, Chelsea Essig & Leonardo Caetano / Unsplash. Festival photographs show past editions, not 2027 creations.
